frames.narration: The orders service sends a heartbeat every second. The monitor keeps the last 100 inter-arrival times: mean 1000 ms, standard deviation 300 ms on this jittery link. Phi is 0.3 right after a beat.
One beat is delayed by a retransmit and arrives 1.8 s after the last. A fixed 2 s timeout almost fired. Phi reached only 2.4, far below the threshold of 8, and the next beat resets it.

A GC pause freezes the service for 6 seconds. No beats arrive. A 2 s fixed timeout declares it dead here. Phi passes 8 after about 2.6 s of silence, so with threshold 8 the monitor becomes suspicious, but it only sees silence, not the pause.

Before acting, the monitor asks a peer to ping the service as well (SWIM ping-req). The peer gets no ack either: the service is frozen, so a second path does not help. The monitor marks it SUSPECT and starts a 5 s grace timer.

The pause ends before the timer. The service hears it is suspected and broadcasts alive with incarnation 8, which beats the rumour about incarnation 7. The suspicion is cleared without an eviction, a failover or a rebalance.
Minutes later the service really crashes. Silence again, but now the peer's ping fails, the monitor's probes fail, and nobody refutes. The 5 s grace timer runs out about 7 s after the last contact.
Verdict: DEAD. A replica is promoted and given a fencing token of 34. The monitor could still be wrong, because a node declared dead may be running somewhere.

If the old instance wakes up and writes with its token 33, storage rejects it. The verdict is only safe because the resource checks the token, not because the detector was right. See leases and fencing tokens.
